comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026–2027 Nanobiology TER Articles 3–5 and 8 control course requirements; the September 2026 chart corroborates their 180 EC. Freshly checked 8 October 2026. English instruction replaces normalized NLD-only metadata, preserving raw NLD provenance and TU Delft/Erasmus University Rotterdam institutional participation. Year one comprises twelve positions totaling 60 EC, with the first formal permissible mixed practical pair NB1430 Molecular Biology Techniques A and NB1445 Biophysics Techniques B, 4 EC each. This is a representative programme assignment, not a free student choice or a prediction of an individual assignment. The alternative is NB1435 plus NB1440; the programme informs students before 1 February 2027 and changes require permission. Year two comprises fourteen required units totaling 60 EC. Current NB2430 Nanotechnology is 3 EC; Article 11.7 prints 4 EC for an older-cohort transition and does not override the current entrant table. Year three is an approved 30-EC minor, NB3000 Bachelor End Project 20 EC and four distinct 2.5-EC electives totaling 10 EC. The electives are the first four formal list entries: NB3015 A Primer in Neuroscience, NB3024 Advanced Math Topics, NB3026 Biomolecular Ultrasound and NB3014 Computational Neuroscience. Selection follows formal order independently of UCR fit; catalogue prerequisites, capacity, enrolment and actual octal availability remain conditions, so this is not an exact future timetable. Outside electives and self-composed minors require Board approval. BEP admission requires all 60 first-year EC plus at least 60 EC from years two and three combined; an approved programme supervisor is required. No alternative pair, minor content or embedded skills adds credits. UCR assessment on 10 October 2026 freshly retrieved the current adopted Appendix and visually inspected the second-/third-year and elective table (PDF p.6), with first-year and project clauses text-checked. The current required courses, representative assigned practical pair, neutral four electives and 180-EC total remain unchanged. Historical transition weights do not override the current entrant table.

core: Cells, biomolecules, genetics, structure/function and laboratory investigation
Mathematical and computational explanation of living systems
Physics, nanoscale measurement and instrumentation in biology
adjacent: Molecular mechanisms of health and disease and fundamental medical research
Neural function and mathematical/computational neuroscience within the selected external elective set

trace: develops computational search and constraint satisfaction for the evidenced biological-modelling direction, complementing numerical and algebraic model-solving methods; it is not a molecular-simulation or biophysics course
develops algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis for computational biological data/model workflows; biological sequence-analysis content is not invented
develops algebraic algorithms, optimisation and mathematical modelling, extending the algorithmic tools available for the target’s quantitative/computational science direction
develops data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation for interpreting biological measurements; disciplinary examples do not imply dedicated genomics training
implements regression and tree-based learning from data, with documented medical examples, to model relationships in biological measurements
implements feature detection, tracking and medical-image analysis, supplying digital analysis of biological images while preserving the absence of optical microscopy/acquisition training

implements artificial neural networks and computer-vision models, supporting computational analysis and the selected neural-network elective connection; artificial networks do not replace biological neurophysiology
develops programming, testing and computational problem-solving as the foundation for the target’s scientific-programming and biological-analysis work
establishes calculus, vectors, matrices and eigenvalues for quantitative biological models
develops matrix methods and linear spaces for representing interacting biological variables and computational models
implements numerical equation solving, integration and differential equations, supplying the actual computational methods for dynamic biological models
extends calculus to several variables, differential equations and complex functions for analysing models of coupled living processes

studies differential-equation, transfer-function and state-space representations of linear systems; these supply specific modelling tools for the evidenced mathematical-biology direction without claiming molecular biophysics
develops probability, parameter estimation and simulation for biological measurements and model uncertainty

studies anatomy through imaging/dissection and structure/function relationships, locating the consequences of cellular disease processes within functioning human systems; it is complementary anatomy rather than nanoscale imaging
studies drug targets, interactions and kinetics, directly connecting molecular processes with therapeutic effects and toxicity
studies immune recognition, receptor development, host-pathogen interactions and immunopathology as molecular/cellular mechanisms of health and disease
investigates molecular and cellular defects causing pathology and their treatments, directly implementing the evidenced molecular-disease direction
studies brain regions and rhythms, evolutionary complexity and research ethics, providing substantive biological content for the selected neuroscience direction
studies neural processing of sensory information and goal-directed action through neuroscience methods, complementing the selected computational-neuroscience direction with biological function
introduces macromolecules, DNA, cells and organ systems, establishing the biological foundation for molecular/quantitative investigation
introduces brain anatomy, brain injury and mental processes as the formal foundation for advanced neural perception/action study
directly studies prokaryotic/eukaryotic cells, current research, reproducibility and laboratory-method modernisation
studies energy handling, homeostasis, signalling and structure/function across organ systems, connecting cellular processes with their organism-level function
studies biomolecule chemistry and metabolic pathways, directly implementing biochemistry and structure/function inquiry
practises biochemical and molecular laboratory work with proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics; nanoscale biophysical instrumentation is outside its documented scope

studies genetic mutations/testing, cell injury, inflammation, repair and neoplasia, directly connecting molecular/cellular structure with malfunction; it is not the full external developmental-biology or molecular-genetics syllabus

alternatives.label: Molecular biology & quantitative living systems
alternatives.concept: Study cells, biomolecules, genetics and experimental biology through substantial mathematical and computational analysis, including neural-system applications supported by the selected external electives. Preserve explicit gaps in nanoscale physics and measurement rather than substituting general science for them.
alternatives.labelReason: Six molecular/physiological biology courses, three neural courses and fourteen mathematical/computational courses implement a quantitative living-systems curriculum. The label does not imply full Nanobiology or nanophysics formation.
progression: All hard workbook gates passed: 24 unique courses / 180 EC, PPD in year one, at least six level-300 courses, formal prerequisites in earlier terms and exact six-term availability. Biology and programming foundations precede laboratory, biochemistry and algorithmic work. Calculus/matrix foundations precede numerical and linear-system methods; Algorithms precedes Advanced Algorithms in the computational alternative. Brain foundations precede Perception & Action. Introductory data methods precede advanced learning/image methods. The open curriculum permits specialised medical work in year two after biology foundations; advisory physiology/biochemistry progression was considered without inventing additional prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Molecular disease mechanisms & quantitative biology
alternatives.concept: Retain molecular/laboratory biology, quantitative modelling and neural function while prioritising pharmacology, immunity, anatomical structure/function and mechanisms of disease instead of advanced algorithmic and neural-network specialisation.
alternatives.labelReason: Four biomedical courses replace algorithmic, optimisation and deep-learning specialisation, yielding a substantial molecular-disease focus with retained quantitative biology; the label makes no nanomedical-device claim.

alternatives.distinctness: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each direction. Algorithms, Advanced Algorithms, Neural Networks & Deep Learning and Optimisation are replaced by Pharmacology, Infection & Immunity, Functional Anatomy and Mechanisms of Disease. This shifts advanced study from computational implementations to biological mechanism and intervention, rather than varying labels or incidental examples.

selection.assessment: Two complete, coherent related programmes pass the course-content, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. The molecular/quantitative core and medical-research direction are supported by independent target evidence; selected neuroscience options inform existing curricula rather than generating an artificial additional route. A nanoscale physics/instrumentation programme cannot be assembled because the workbook lacks mechanics/optics, molecular/statistical biophysics, soft matter, electronic measurement and nanofabrication progression. General image processing or mathematical models cannot be relabelled as these subjects. No third programme is manufactured.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives combine molecular and cellular biology, laboratory work and quantitative/computational methods, with neural or molecular-disease applications. They preserve substantial gaps in nanoscale physics, microscopy/acquisition, biophysical instruments, soft matter and nanotechnology, and do not represent full Nanobiology equivalence.
